methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents distributed capacity-building outside metro corridors, creating peer learning infrastructure that could spread deeper AI fluency through leadership networks in underserved regions.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly address the distribution problem through grassroots knowledge transfer, signaling potential for peer-to-peer skill diffusion that builds depth beyond platform adoption.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student commentary explicitly identifying data centers as exacerbating urban-rural divides signals awareness that infrastructure concentration without capability distribution creates economic extraction rather than empowerment.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Specialized summer program targeting visually impaired students in tech/cybersecurity demonstrates Richmond developing niche excellence in inclusive AI education, but program-based approach suggests limited scalability beyond concentrated resources.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding AI minor to curriculum creates distributed knowledge infrastructure through alumni networks radiating from New River Valley, potentially seeding deeper technical fluency across regions where graduates settle.
